# Module `core`

core::aspects - Standard polymorphic contracts

The six canonical core aspects define Vyb's standard behavior contracts:
stringification (Display), debugging output (Debug), value cloning (Clone),
and equality/comparison/hashing (Equatable / Comparable / Hashable). They are
the aspect-side surface that collections (e.g. HashMap<K, V> with
`Hashable + Equatable` bounds), the Iterator protocol, and generic algorithms
constrain against. Comparable refines Equatable, so any type that binds
Comparable must also bind Equatable.

<a id="sym-stringops"></a>
### `StringOps` · aspect

```
aspect StringOps {
    split(self<String>, sep<String>)<Vec<String>>
    index_of(self<String>, needle<String>)<Int>
}
```

StringOps - String manipulation helpers layered on the built-in String methods.
`.split(sep)` returns a `Vec<String>` of the parts between each occurrence of
`sep` in `self` (an empty `sep` yields a single-element Vec holding the whole
string; leading/trailing/consecutive separators produce empty parts, matching
the common split semantics). Bound to String and always available, since this
module is auto-imported into user programs.

<a id="file-stdlib-core-iter-vyb"></a>
**File: `stdlib/core/iter.vyb`**

core::iter - the standard iteration protocol.

`Iterator` is Vyb's single iteration contract (see the [DECIDED] aspect-based
design in TODO.md). A type binds it, assigns the associated `type Item` (what
the iterator yields), and implements `next`, which returns the native optional
`Self::Item?` -- present (the bare payload) for each element, absent when the
sequence is exhausted. The receiver is taken by reference
(`self<their<Self>>`) so `next` can advance internal cursor state in place on
the caller's object.

A bound iterator is consumed by calling `.next()` in a loop with the native
optional surface (present binds the bare value, `?` is the absent arm):

  import core::iter

  while (true) {
      match (it.next()) {
          v -> { ... use v ... }
          ?  -> { break }
      }
  }

`for (item in it)` desugars to exactly that `.next()` / `match` loop.

This module is explicitly imported (`import core::iter`) — it is not part of the
auto-imported core contracts module (`core::aspects`), so bind authors keep full
control over when the `Iterator` name is in scope.

<a id="sym-iterator"></a>
### `Iterator` · aspect

```
aspect Iterator {
    next(self<their<Self>>)<Self::Item ?>
}
```

<a id="file-stdlib-core-math-vyb"></a>
**File: `stdlib/core/math.vyb`**

core::math - numeric composition helpers.

Vyb's math intrinsics (`abs`, `sqrt`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `exp`, `log`,
`log2`, `log10`, `pow`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `min`, `max`) are built in
and available everywhere without an import. This module layers small helper
functions over those intrinsics for common numeric patterns, giving numeric
code a single, explicit import surface. It is explicitly imported — it is not
part of the auto-imported core contracts module (`core::aspects`).
